text:
ajay: FYI ran a weight-only 8-bit pass using bitsandbytes / llm.int8 on rwt-13b (checkpoint rwt-13b-v2) across our p3 fleet. quick summary: big latency win, small quality deltas on some slices. attaching run notes below.

maria: nice — which evals did you run? overall perf numbers?

ajay: ran eval slices: summarization (news long), closed-book QA (open domain), instruction-following (LLM-Bench subset). numbers: FP16 baseline perplexity=10.2, INT8=10.9 (~6.9% relative increase). rouge-l (news) drops ~4.5 pts absolute on the longest summaries (>1024). EM on QA slice -3.2 pts absolute. latency: token-latency down from ~140ms -> ~100ms (28% faster) at batch=1 on p3.8x throughputs +34% with same batch config. GPU memory reduction ~37%.

kevin: that perf delta / quality tradeoff is inline with expectations. did you use per-channel scaling or the default bnb recipe?

ajay: used bnb v0.39 default weight-only (per-row scaling) + fp16 activations. conversion command was basically:
```
python -m tools.convert_bnb --model rwt-13b-v2 --target 8 --weight_only --keep_fp16_acts --output rwt-13b-int8-bnb
```
Also experimented with `--group-size 128` and `--group-size 2048`. group-size=128 reduced rouge drop by ~0.8 pts but increased memory slightly.

ciara: any sign of layer-specific regressions? sometimes first few transformer blocks blow up with 8-bit.

ajay: good call — saw outsized quality delta concentrated in layers 0-3 and final linear head on the summarization slice. GPT-style QA mostly ok. Looking at weight histograms, those early layers have heavy-tailed distributions that the per-row scaling doesn't capture.

maria: did you try fallback for those layers? (gptq / fp16)

ajay: yes — two experiments: 1) mixed precision fallback (keep layers 0-3 fp16) -> rouge drop halved, latency penalty ~+6% vs full-int8. 2) GPTQ-quantized early layers (per-channel learned scales) -> quality almost matches fp16 but conversion time & complexity jumped. For production simple mixed-fp fallback seems lowest-friction.

kevin: anything weird with KV cache or long-context inference?

ajay: interestingly, beyond 2048 tokens we see occasional weird repetition in int8 runs on the instruction slice. hypothesis: kv cache accumulation + quantization rounding creates tiny drift in logits that compounds. reproducer attached in the runnotes.

ciara: can you paste the minimal repro?

ajay: sure:
```
# repro snippet (python)
from rwt_infer import Client
c = Client(model='rwt-13b-int8', max_length=4096)
prompt = 'Summarize: ' + 'A'*3000 + '\nTL;DR:'
print(c.generate(prompt, temperature=0.2))
```
full fp16 run yields concise TL;DR, int8 sometimes repeats 'A' chunk then truncates.

maria: thanks. for rollout plan I suggest: canary 2% traffic to int8 profile, route short-context (<=512) requests preferentially to int8, long-context to fp16. add a regression alert on rouge/EM with 24h window and a qps/latency metric change.

ajay: agreed. also added a model-profile config we can use in routing: `profile: {name: "rwt-13b-int8-lowlatency", max_context: 512, fallback: "rwt-13b-fp16", canary: 0.02}`.

kevin: do we have automated evals hooked into the console to catch these per-slice drops?

ciara: not yet for the new summarization slice. i've queued a nightly job to run knife-edge evals (summarize-long, qa-hallucination, instruction-fidelity) against any new quantized build. will add thresholds to alert to pager/signal.

deploy-bot: deploy started: rwt-13b-int8-bnb -> staging (tags: int8-bnb-2026-03-20).

maria: final ask — can you add the conversion artifacts (scale params, group-size) + a small visual of layer histograms to the run folder? ops needs that to reproduce on Private.

ajay: done. saved to s3://rwt-evals/int8/1801234567/ with `conversion.json`, `layer_hist.png`, and `eval-report.json`.

ciara: follow-ups: 1) try AWQ / GPTQ for early-layer fallback to compare compute vs quality, 2) test group-size sweep 64/128/512, 3) record per-token latency tail (p99/p999) for both profiles. i'll schedule and tag owners.

kevin: perfect. thanks ajay — super actionable. :thumbsup:

ajay: any objections to promoting to Dedicated canary after 48h with current routing rules?
maria: no objections, as long as alerts + rollback playbook are in place.

ciara: put the rollback playbook in the run folder as well. noted.

ajay: ok moving forward with canary tomorrow morning 08:00 UTC. will post an update after 24h metrics.

maria: cheers, keep us posted.
